Staszow New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Staszów, Poland

Not demolished. Established in 1819 to replace the old cemetery closed for sanitary reasons (see the Staszów Old Jewish Cemetery record for the town's fuller community history), this newer cemetery received its first burials in 1825. Germans used its tombstones to pave streets and courtyards during WWII; postwar residents continued removing stones for construction. Holocaust survivor Jacek Goldfarb funded a major early-1990s restoration, fencing the site and building a lapidarium; roughly 150 recovered tombstones found at the former Gestapo headquarters on Kościelna Street were returned here. A 1992 monument marks the 50th anniversary of the ghetto's liquidation over its 1942 mass grave; in 2002, remains of two people discovered during a house renovation on Kościelna Street were reburied here beneath a matzevah-style monument.
